The standard algorithm (from supports-color):
- If `FORCE_COLOR` set: 0/false -> none, 1/true -> basic, 2 -> 256, 3 -> truecolor
- If `NO_COLOR` set or `NODE_DISABLE_COLORS` -> none
- If `TERM=dumb` or `TERM` undefined -> none
- If `--no-color` flag -> none
- If `--color` flag -> basic/truecolor
- If not TTY -> none (unless CI detection)
- Windows: check for ANSICON, ConEmu, WT_SESSION, TERM_PROGRAM, etc.
- CI: check CI env vars
- COLORTERM truecolor/24bit -> truecolor
- TERM contains 256color -> 256
- else basic

- `src/color-support.js` — `getColorSupport(stream?)` returns `{level, supported, hasBasic, has256, has16m}` (0–3), honoring `FORCE_COLOR`, `NO_COLOR`/`NODE_DISABLE_COLORS`, `--color[=256|16m|never]` flags, `TERM`/`COLORTERM`, TTY, Windows consoles, and CI. Also exports `supportsColor()`.
- `src/index.js` — `createColors(stream?)` wraps detection with safe ANSI styles that no-op when unsupported.
- `bin/cli.js` — executable entry (`colorful`) that reports the detected level and prints a styled message only when supported.
- `test/color-support.test.js` — 9 tests, all passing (`npm test`).
